review_candidates.description: Overview The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems. CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally. At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture. Program Overview Uganda has made significant progress in reducing maternal and neonatal mortality since 2016, with maternal mortality declining by 44% from 338 to 189 deaths per 100,000 live births and neonatal mortality by 18.5% from 27 to 22 deaths per 1,000 live births. However, mortality remains unacceptably high, driven by causes such as birth asphyxia, prematurity, and maternal hemorrhage, with many deaths resulting from delays in recognizing danger signs, seeking care, reaching capable facilities, and receiving timely treatment. Strengthening emergency referral systems is therefore critical and requires functional communication and transport linkages, improved triage and referral protocols, and timely, safe transfer of women and newborns requiring emergency care. CHAI Uganda’s Sexual, Reproductive, Maternal and Newborn Health (SRMNH) Program partners with the Ministry of Health to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality by expanding access to priority family planning, maternal and newborn health products and services, while strengthening emergency referral pathways at community, health facility, and district levels. Relationship Management Build and maintain strong working relationships with Ministry of Health Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) department and the Emergency Medical Services (EMS) department leads, district health teams, health facility managers, and community structures engaged in emergency referral. Provide technical assistance to government counterparts in the development and implementation of national and district-level emergency referral guidelines and protocols. Coordinate with other SRMNH workstream teams (monitoring, evaluation and learning, supply chain, and service delivery) to ensure integrated approaches to emergency referral system strengthening. Engage with partner organizations and donors to share learnings, coordinate activities, and ensure alignment with national referral system priorities. Represent CHAI in relevant technical working groups and stakeholder forums related to emergency obstetric and neonatal care. Strategic Communication Synthesize complex data and field findings into clear, actionable insights and recommendations for diverse audiences including government officials, donors, and internal teams. Prepare high-quality program reports, presentations, case studies, and other knowledge products on emergency referral systems interventions and outcomes. Contribute to the development of abstracts, success stories, and lessons learned documents for external dissemination. Develop concept notes and funding proposals to support the expansion and sustainability of emergency referral systems interventions, in collaboration with the Program Manager and relevant stakeholders. Financial Management Collaborate with the Program Manager to track expenditures related to emergency referral systems activities and ensure appropriate grant reporting. Lead the development of activity budgets and ensure that program activities are implemented in line with approved workplans and financial plans. Problem-Solving Conduct landscape assessments and situational analyses to identify gaps in emergency referral pathways for mothers and newborns across community, facility, and district levels. Technical Provide technical input to the design and rollout of emergency referral protocols, triage tools, referral forms, and communication systems (e.g., community-to-facility and facility-to-facility referral). Support the assessment and strengthening of transport and communication mechanisms for obstetric and neonatal emergencies, including community ambulance schemes, motorcycle ambulances, and facility communication tools. Contribute to the mapping of emergency referral networks, including identification of EmONC-capable facilities, referral routes, and community linkage structures. Lead the development of training materials and facilitate capacity building sessions for health workers (including community health workers), and district health teams on emergency referral protocols and communication systems. We operate eight brands across seven markets in the UK, US, Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands, Italy and Spain. Every year, 1.7 million pets and horses find a new home through our platforms, and some of our flagship platforms include Pets4Homes.co.uk, Deine-Tierwelt.de and Lancasterpuppies.com. The pet rehoming experience has remained largely unchanged for decades. At PMG, we are on a mission to transform this process by making it more trusted, safe and convenient through innovative technology. We are a driven and ambitious team with a track record of building unicorns, backed by top-tier investors such as Verdane. As a company, we have been profitable since our first year, meaning we do not rely on investor capital for our growth. The opportunity This is our first dedicated PR hire and it covers the whole group. Over the years, PMG has managed to reduce animal welfare issues on our platforms far below any peer, through ID verification of breeders, AI-assisted moderation of adverts, a zero-tolerance approach to illegal puppy imports and unlicensed high-volume breeding, and by going far beyond what the law requires. Your job is to tell the world about it. We know the playbook works because we have already done it once. In the UK, we have changed the public conversation about Pets4Homes from risky classifieds to the most trusted and responsible way to find a pet. Our annual Pet Industry Report is now a fixture in the national press and TV. The challenge is doing that in more than one market at a time. That is the job: take a proven single-market playbook and make it run in seven, as one person backed by AI tools and outside help where needed, rather than a department. Your edge is finding the story inside the data and knowing exactly which angle will make a journalist stop scrolling. You bring an AI-forward mindset, the instinct to ask how can I leverage myself through AI, and you use it daily for data analysis, drafting, localising, and getting a story out across markets, so covering seven markets does not mean seven times the work. What You Will Do Turn our marketplace data into publishable stories: pricing and demand trends, breed rankings, most popular puppy names, buyer surveys on preferences and the like. One shared instrument based on real-time data and identical core survey questions across markets. Build and run the group editorial calendar, planned per market around seasonal hooks such as heatwaves, fireworks, International Puppy Day and so on, so we are ready before the news cycle asks. Own our trust and safety transparency reporting: listings blocked, scams intercepted, buyer money protected, illegal import patterns by origin, for distribution to journalists and animal welfare stakeholders alike. Mine breeder reviews, Trustpilot and support conversations for the human stories regional press actually run. Become PMG's press desk, so the journalist relationship belongs to PMG rather than to an agency. Brief and equip country leads and founders as spokespeople: talking points, Q&A, data appendices, prep before interviews. Requirements Must-have experience 5+ years in PR, communications or journalism, preferably in-house, with coverage in national or major regional media that you personally landed. Data journalism experience is a strong plus. A track record of building stories out of data rather than distributing press releases. You can spot the angle a journalist will want before they ask, and you are comfortable enough with spreadsheets and dashboards to find it yourself and sanity check a number before a reporter does. Daily, active use of AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT for research, drafting, localisation and workflow automation. You think in terms of how to leverage yourself through AI, not around it, with a clear view of what to automate and what stays human. Native-level English, written to a standard that needs no editing before it reaches a journalist. Able to operate as a team of one: briefing agencies and freelancers and holding them to account, rather than managing staff beneath you. Preferable Experience Experience in a reputation-exposed marketplace, such as pets, dating, gambling, fintech or the gig economy, or in a category under active regulatory or campaigner scrutiny. Experience running consumer surveys with panels or survey tools. Digital PR fundamentals: earned links, newsjacking, syndication. You will thrive here if you Have the mindset of a hands-on builder rather than a delegator. Believe process serves outcomes, not the other way around. Value clarity, candour and collaboration. Are excited by the challenge of scaling one of Europe's most impactful consumer marketplaces. What We Offer A function that does not exist yet, yours to design, across seven markets, with a proven UK playbook to build from. A proprietary dataset covering millions of pet and horse transactions that no journalist can get anywhere else. Direct access to founders and country leads. A profitable, growing business rather than a slide deck. A diverse team of more than 100 colleagues across the world. Competitive compensation.
